Put simply, it's an attack where the target computer is bombarded with needless requests in an effort to overload it, crash it, and prevent people from accessing that network or machine. So, the most important thing to do to guard against DDoS attacks is to separate network data as soon as possible. In this study, we provide a new approach to intrusion detection algorithms known as CNN-GRU Attention. It combines Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), & a self-attention mechanism to improve algorithm accuracy. The model's structure is intended to effectively represent the geographical and temporal aspects of network flows. The experimental findings highlight the effectiveness of deep learning in cybersecurity applications, outperforming standard models. The experimental outcome showed that suggested hybrid model outperformed the competition on CICDDoS2019 data set, suggesting that it might be useful for detecting and categorising DDoS attack traffic. We evaluated the proposed system compared to state-of-the-art models. We are pleased to report that the accuracy of our work was 99.6%.

articleTitle: Blockchain Technology and Data Privacy: A Comprehensive Review and Future Perspective
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Due to its decentralized and impervious to tampering nature, blockchain technology presents great opportunities for improving data privacy in a variety of contexts. This study offers a thorough analysis of the body of research on the subject of blockchain technology and data privacy. It explores privacy concerns in blockchain systems, clarifies privacy-preserving techniques, and examines their application in diverse contexts such as healthcare, IoT, crowdsensing, and federated learning. The paper highlights the challenges associated with blockchain-based privacy solutions, including data immutability, transparency, and scalability, and identifies emerging trends and opportunities for future research. This paper attempts to offer important insights into how blockchain technology can change the data privacy environment in our networked and data-driven society through a thorough analysis. Lastly, new developments and issues are addressed, including self-sovereign identification and integration with machine learning. Future research is encouraged to focus on issues like scalability, standardization, legal frameworks, and user education.

articleTitle: CredVault: A Credential Management System based on Zero-Knowledge Proofs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: As digital identities become increasingly valuable and vulnerable, the protection of personal credentials has become a critical concern. This paper introduces a fresh perspective on credential management, focusing on enhancing privacy and security. We propose a user-centric approach that revolves around the idea of creating a safe space for digital credentials within decentralized wallets. By leveraging existing social login mechanisms and establishing secure tokenized containers for credentials, users can securely store and manage their digital identity. Our framework aims to empower individuals by providing them with control over their credentials while minimizing the risk of exposure to third parties. This paper outlines the core concepts and objectives of our approach, highlighting its potential to revolutionize the way we manage and protect our digital identities.

articleTitle: Blockchain for IoT/Industrial IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: With the Increased demand of IoT technology now day’s the data integrity also major factor of considerations by many researchers. Blockchain is one of the best suitable solutions used to provide data integrity through tamper-proof ledgers. Decentralized operation leads peer to peer communication between IoT devices. Blockchain technology enhances Industrial IoT by providing a secure, decentralized, and transparent framework for data management, security, and automation. It enables new business models, improves operational efficiency, and fosters trust among stakeholders in IoT ecosystems. The work mentioned in the paper gives the insight about critical challenges addressed by blockchain, types, platforms, characteristics, factors for experimenting and Security threats to IoT are mentioned. This paper outlines a research roadmap for the integration of blockchain technology into IoT and Industrial IoT (IIoT) which will add significant contribution in the research and innovation.

articleTitle: Investigating Cyber Threats against Proof-of-work Blockchain Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In recent years, blockchain networks have become a singular power in the financial sector. Proof of work (POW) networks are among the most significant and widespread kinds of blockchain networks. One of the main issues POW blockchains have been dealing with recently is cyber threats. Targets and a market segment have been impacted by cyberattacks against multiple well-known initiatives in this field. In this sense, several attacks have been examined and researched in these kinds of networks with the goal of finding important information and roots. Furthermore, the Ethereum (POW) network is analyzed using 140 actual attacks as a sample. The study's findings demonstrate the numerous similarities among various attacks. Additionally, variations are apparent.

articleTitle: Raspberry Pi Powered Deep Learning-based Chest X-ray Analysis for Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Despite the impressive performance, traditional medical imaging analysis equipment is often costly and cumbersome, limiting accessibility, especially in remote or resource-constrained areas. This work proposes harnessing the capabilities of deep learning models, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). This study explores the feasibility of employing CNN models, particularly ResNet family, which have demonstrated exceptional performance in various deep learning applications. In this work, CNN is applied for the detection of lung diseases by considering chest X-rays and automatically classifying them into four categories: COVID-19, pneumonia, lung opacity, and normal. Furthermore, the research investigates the implementation of the trained CNN model on a Raspberry Pi, a low-cost, single-board computer with decent computational power. By deploying the model on such an accessible platform, the aim is to extend the benefits of deep learning-based chest X-ray analysis to resource-limited environments. The proposed model was able to achieve 97.98% classification accuracy and demonstrated significant potential in classifying chest X-ray images. The integration of efficient deep learning architectures contributes to the development of robust diagnostic capabilities, potentially revolutionizing healthcare accessibility in underserved regions.

articleTitle: A Survey on Harnessing High-Performance Computing and Machine Learning for Detecting Stealthy Cache-Based Side-Channel Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: This survey investigates different approaches to improve the ability of cloud systems to withstand cache-based side-channel attacks, with a primary emphasis on real-time detection capabilities and the ability to identify stealth attacks, incorporating machine learning and High-Performance Computing (HPC) techniques. The study categorises the security measures into hardware, hypervisor, and two-stage strategies. Additionally, the research assesses the effectiveness, accuracy, and impact of various defence mechanisms on cloud systems, specifically considering High-Performance Computing (HPC). The main objectives include analysing the occurrence of false-positive results, evaluating the impact of defences on cloud security and performance, and assessing the feasibility of employing machine learning and HPC for detecting stealth attacks in real-time.

articleTitle: Automated Energy Transaction and Incentivization of Prosumers and Consumers through Smart Contracts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: World’s population is rapidly expanding, and so is the need for an uninterrupted power supply. Along with this, there is also a rapid rise in tech-savvy initiatives and industrialization. All these lead to an increase in the carbon footprint, thereby resulting in an increasingly polluted world. Most governments, regardless of their politics, are pledging to reduce their carbon emissions and shift to greener energy resources. Integrating renewable energy (RE) into the current energy system is a key step in that direction, but the existing energy infrastructure is incapable of incorporating RE sources and catering to the rising demands without technological interventions. Electricity obtained through RE is very volatile and subject to environmental conditions. In such a scenario, the RE alone would not be able to support the grid at peak demand times. Grid would need additional support in the form of demand response (DR). DR incentivizes consumers to reduce their electricity usage during peak demand, but calculating the real-time data of all the consumers and rewarding them becomes a hassle without smart, secure, and reliable communication and storage systems. Hence, to enhance participant trust and automate the entire DR process, blockchain and smart contracts (SC) are viable solutions due to their transparency and immutability. This paper works on a SC-based DR programme to incentivize users based on their choices using an ethereum test network (testnet).

articleTitle: Blockchain Applications in Facilitating Secure and Efficient Energy Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In modern power systems, we are directing towards green energy and carbon-neutral emission targets. One of the solutions to this issue is the integration of renewable with the existing power system. Blockchain plays a vital role in secure and efficient energy transactions and grid management. Today, several technologies or trading platforms are available that provide affordable, clean, and reliable energy and help implement automatic real-time monitoring and billing. From these the overall operating cost is reduced and makes our system capable to manage outages and demands more efficiently. Among them, one of the most trusted technologies is Blockchain Technology, which offers a trustworthy environment for the participants to communicate with each other securely. This paper summarises several blockchain technology applications in power system operations. The motive is to provide in-depth knowledge of energy transaction management, automated metering and billing systems, and security enhancement.

articleTitle: Preserving the Veracity of Digital Media using Neural Network Based Detection of Deepfake Videos
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Free deep learning applications have made it easier to create similar to humans synthesized videos in the past couple of years, a trend known as "deep fakes." Over many years, it has been possible to manipulate digital videos through the skilful use of visual effects. However, the simplicity with which fake content can be created and its realism have both increased dramatically due to recent advancements in deep learning. It is easy to imagine scenarios in which people are blackmailed, political unrest is caused, or events involving terrorism are fabricated using these realistic face-swapping deepfakes. This project proposal describes an exciting deep learning-based method that effectively recognizes real videos from ones produced by artificial intelligence. The use of artificial intelligence (AI) to combat AI is mentioned in the proposed model. The proposed method extracts frame-level features utilizing a Res-Next Convolution neural network. These attributes are then used to train an LSTM-based Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to identify videos based on whether they have been altered or not, i.e., whether they are deepfake or real. The Deepfake Detection Challenge and Celeb-DF are two examples of the many available datasets that are combined to create a big, balanced, and mixed dataset that the model's performance on real-time data and apply it to real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: SDN Security: Taming the Wild West of Network Automation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Software-Defined Networking (SDN) has revolutionized computer networking by enabling unprecedented levels of programmability, flexibility, and centralized control. However, the distinctive architecture of SDN introduces novel security challenges that must be addressed to maintain the integrity and reliability of these networks. This paper offers a detailed analysis of the security issues inherent in SDN environments, focusing on vulnerabilities in the centralized control plane, programmable interfaces, and the separation between control and data planes.To address these challenges, the paper proposes a multi-layered security strategy, encompassing measures such as access control, secure communication protocols, flow rule verification, and secure application development. Additionally, it explores key security frameworks and tools tailored for SDN, including methods for security monitoring, incident response, and rigorous testing and validation practices.Through case studies and real-world examples, the paper highlights the practical implementation of SDN security measures in various settings, underscoring both the benefits and the complexities involved. The discussion also extends to future research directions, particularly the security implications of emerging technologies like intent-based networking, network slicing, and edge computing. The paper concludes by recommending a holistic approach to SDN security, emphasizing the importance of automation, open standards, and collaborative efforts to ensure a secure and resilient network infrastructure.

articleTitle: Empowering Accessibility: AI-driven Laser-Controlled Robotic Hand for Enhanced Independence
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: This paper introduces a groundbreaking assistive technology, a Laser-Controlled Robotic Hand, designed to address the unique challenges faced by physically challenged individuals. Leveraging laser technology for precise and intuitive control, the proposed system aims to empower users with limited motor function to regain autonomy in their daily lives. The Laser-Controlled Robotic Hand incorporates a sophisticated actuation mechanism, responsive to laser-generated gestures. These gestures, interpreted through advanced image processing, enable users to seamlessly manipulate the robotic hand with remarkable accuracy. The system prioritizes accessibility, offering a customizable user interface adaptable to individual needs and preferences. Experimental validation, including usability studies involving physically challenged individuals, showcases the effectiveness of the Laser-Controlled Robotic Hand. Performance metrics such as accuracy, response time, and user satisfaction underscore the potential impact of this technology on enhancing the quality of life for individuals with physical disabilities. Beyond its immediate applications in daily tasks, the system holds promise for rehabilitation purposes and can be further optimized through collaboration with healthcare professionals. The paper concludes with a discussion on potential future directions, emphasizing the ongoing commitment to innovation in assistive technology for the benefit of a diverse range of users.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis Attack on RSA using various Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Cryptanalysis systematically exploits vulnerabilities in cryptographic algorithms to decrypt ciphertext without access to the private key. This study leverages neural networks, which excel in identifying intricate patterns within large datasets, for cryptanalysis of RSA-encrypted text. Specifically, it investigates the use of various neural network architectures, including Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), and Transformers, to generate decrypted text from encrypted inputs. The objective is to evaluate the effectiveness of these models in performing sequence-to-sequence tasks relevant to cryptanalysis. The experimental setup involves training and testing these models on a dataset generated by RSA encryption of an English language corpus using various key sizes. Results indicate varying levels of success across different architectures, with Transformers showing the best performance. This research contributes to understanding the applicability of neural networks in cryptanalysis and highlights their potential to identify vulnerabilities in cryptographic systems.

articleTitle: CoverS: Smart Contract-based Secure and Reliable Framework for V2V Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Communication between vehicles, known as Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication, plays a critical role in enhancing traffic management and road safety by facilitating the real-time exchange of vital information. While traditional methods like Dedicated Short-Range Communication (DSRC) and Long-Term Evolution (LTE) have proven effective, they are not without limitations, particularly concerning privacy and security. Emerging technologies such as 5G and Blockchain offer promising solutions to address these challenges. This study explores the integration of Blockchain technology into V2V communication systems to improve data security, reliability, and privacy. Blockchain’s decentralized nature inherently ensures data integrity and transparency, while smart contracts automate processes, guaranteeing secure and efficient data transmission. The proposed framework targets the optimization of V2V communication by leveraging Blockchain’s unique features, including data security, immutability, and decentralization. The primary objective is to develop a Blockchain-enabled system that facilitates secure communication channels between vehicles. This system will incorporate functionalities such as user and vehicle registration, authentication, and efficient communication algorithms. This research contributes significantly to the establishment of a robust V2V communication framework, ultimately paving the way for improved road safety and traffic management.

articleTitle: HealthLink: A Cutting-Edge System for Secure Healthcare Data with IoT, Blockchain, and IPFS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In today's rapidly evolving healthcare landscape, the integration of cutting-edge technologies such as IoT and wearable devices has led to significant advancements, particularly in the realm of remote patient monitoring. Despite these advancements, the traditional client/server architecture prevalent in current implementations presents substantial challenges related to security and privacy, leaving healthcare systems vulnerable to various attacks. Consequently, stringent regulatory and security measures are imperative to safeguard health data. To address these challenges and meet regulatory requirements, transitioning to a distributed architecture is essential. Blockchain technology, renowned for its distributed nature and robust security features, offers a promising solution to mitigate the security risks inherent in IoT-based systems. Motivated by these considerations, this study introduces HealthLink—a secure healthcare framework that seamlessly integrates IoT and Blockchain technologies.HealthLink is designed to facilitate remote patient monitoring, particularly for chronic diseases that require continuous oversight. The framework prioritizes security, scalability, and processing efficiency. Security measures include the use of re-encryption proxies combined with Blockchain for hash data storage, while access control is managed through smart contracts. To enhance Blockchain scalability, an off-chain IPFS-based database is employed for data storage, and the Ethereum Blockchain-based proof of authority is leveraged to expedite data storage processes. As a practical demonstration, we apply the HealthLink system to diabetes management, presenting execution results through system interfaces. Experimental findings highlight substantial enhancements in the security of healthcare systems compared to conventional methodologies, underscoring the potential of HealthLink to revolutionize remote patient monitoring and data security in healthcare.

articleTitle: Security Assessment Framework and Evaluation for Blockchain Applications (SAFE-Block)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In the rapidly changing technologies, blockchain is gaining traction for revolutionizing industries with its decentralized mechanism to transform traditional business processes. As the number of decentralized apps and associated threats increased, we introduced a security assessment framework for blockchain-based applications to detect security flaws in decentralized systems. The approach covers user access control, secure data handling, and ensuring the safety and reliability of data throughout its lifecycle. This framework boosts blockchain-based application security through best practices for APIs, consensus algorithms, and smart contract development. Supports security evaluations for the database and docker components, ensuring a complete approach to decentralized system security. It offers a security overview and empowers organizations to confidently adopt and develop blockchain-based Applications, enhancing trust and security in decentralized environments.

articleTitle: Leveraging AI for Enhanced Botnet Detection - A Review of Machine Learning Approach for Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Botnets represent a substantial threat to cybersecurity, enabling malicious actors to execute large-scale attacks that compromise network integrity and data confidentiality. Current detection methods often fall short in addressing the rapidly evolving strategies employed by botnets. This study has an aim of designing and developing a sophisticated botnet detection system leveraging artificial intelligence (AI) techniques. By integrating machine learning algorithms and advanced data analysis methods, the proposed system seeks to accurately identify and mitigate botnet activities in real-time. The study will evaluate the effectiveness of various AI models in detecting botnet traffic, provide a comparative analysis of their performance, and propose an optimal framework for implementation in cybersecurity infrastructures.

articleTitle: Unveiling the Invisible Threat: Using Machine Learning to Detect Credit Card Fraud
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Businesses, including both conventional brick-and-mortar businesses and internet firms, have faced particular hurdles as a result of the COVID-19 epidemic. Online commerce has become more prevalent as a result of the installation of movement restrictions that made it more difficult to make physical purchases. However, a rise in online credit card theft has coincided with this transformation, undermining customer confidence in online transactions. As a result, there is a compelling need to create a machine learning framework that is incredibly strong and can successfully identify almost all cases of fraudulent credit card activity.Our research aims to identify 100% of fraudulent and scam-related credit card transactions, which is an ambitious target. Within the larger category, these fraudulent events are a sizable fraction. Our research focuses on improving data preprocessing as a solution to this.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Intrusion Detection Techniques Using Stack Ensemble Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In the dynamic realm of cybersecurity, ensuring efficient intrusion detection is crucial for safeguarding networks and systems from malevolent actions, dangers, and unauthorised entry. Conventional detection technologies, such as firewalls and systems based on signatures, have limitations when it comes to dealing with dynamic and complex threats. This research investigates the use of stack ensemble machine learning methods to improve intrusion detection systems (IDS). This strategy enhances detection accuracy, robustness, and scalability by amalgamating many base models into a meta-learner, thereby capitalising on the benefits of different approaches. The technique encompasses the process of preparing data, performing cross-validation, and selecting base learners, resulting in notable enhancements in the identification and mitigation of cyber risks. The suggested stack ensemble model has exceptional performance in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, obtaining an overall detection accuracy of 98.7%. The results emphasise the potential of stack ensemble approaches in enhancing the capabilities of IDS, offering a dependable and scalable solution for contemporary cybersecurity concerns.

articleTitle: Integrated Approach for Video Frame Dehazing and Living Being Detection for Fire Case Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: This research presents a sophisticated deep learning-based framework designed to improve visibility and detect living beings in environments affected by fire. The proposed method operates in two key phases: first, the dehazing and desmoking of images and video frames, and second, the detection of living beings within these enhanced visuals. The initial phase leverages the Feature Fusion Attention Network (FFA-Net) to effectively eliminate haze and smoke, resulting in significantly clearer and more detailed imagery. The second phase employs the YOLOv8 object detection model, known for its precision and speed, to accurately identify and localize living beings within the processed images. This integrated approach ensures that the visual data is both clear and that the detection process is timely and accurate, which is crucial for coordinating rescue efforts in disaster scenarios. The proposed method has been rigorously tested across various datasets and environmental conditions, demonstrating superior performance in both image enhancement and detection accuracy, making it a reliable tool for improving situational awareness and supporting decision-making in fire rescue operations.

articleTitle: Optimizing Job Search: A Multi-Model Approach with DRNN-BES, Collaborative Filtering, and LLM-NER Resume Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative job recommendation platform designed to optimize the job search process through advanced technology integration. The platform features a sophisticated Resume Analyzer leveraging NLP and ML to meticulously extract candidate information. Coupled with a Recommendation System that employs mixture models such as DRNN-BES and collaborative filtering, it delivers personalized job suggestions tailored to individual profiles. Additionally, the system utilizes state-of-the-art web scraping technologies to continuously update its database with diverse and current job listings from various online sources, ensuring a wide range of opportunities are accessible. This integration of technologies not only refines job-matching precision but also significantly improves the efficiency of connecting job seekers with appropriate opportunities. Initial experimental results underscore the enhanced effectiveness and accuracy of our recommendation system, particularly when incorporating user behavioral data into the collaborative filtering algorithm. This paper demonstrates the transformative potential of integrating AI into job seeking, offering a scalable, unbiased, and time-efficient approach to modern employment challenges.

articleTitle: A Systematic Study On Cloud Forensic Framework, Challenges And Technologies Used For Evidence Preservation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: In this study we have focused on 3 research questions and tried to do analysis of that questions. The term "cloud computing" is wide yet ambiguous, encompassing a range of dynamically allocated services. Cloud computing can be seen as having two benefits and drawbacks for forensic analysis and legal applications. On the one hand, obtaining digital evidence from cloud sources could pose challenging legal and technological issues across jurisdictions. One potential remedy for these issues is the cloud forensic zero trust concept. A diligent and critical attitude to security is required when using the zero-trust model for cloud forensics, since no user or device can be considered completely trustworthy. In this paper we have proposed a zero trust model for security of evidence in cloud forensic. Cloud forensic investigations are crucial for identifying and analysing security incidents within cloud environments. By adopting a least privilege approach, organizations can minimize the attack surface and limit potential exposure to security risks. Additionally, leveraging encryption and strong identity management practices further strengthens the security of cloud forensic processes. Organizations may proactively identify and address security events in their cloud environments by combining threat detection tools and advanced security analytics. This proactive strategy improves the overall security posture and increases the efficacy of forensic investigations. This study outlined a number of debate points that paved the path for technological advancement in the future when it comes to crime scene evidence.

articleTitle: An Effect of Machine Learning based Algorithm for Identify Android Malware
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Malware is a substantial challenge in operating systems and software, and the Android system is no exception to this pervasive issue. Despite the array of existing detection and analysis techniques, accurately identifying new malware remains a persistent challenge. This paper aims to delve into and shed light on the prevailing detection and analysis methodologies employed for identifying malicious code in the Android ecosystem. In addition to exploring existing methods, the architecture proposes the utilization of machine learning algorithms for a more robust analysis of such malware, complemented by semantic analysis. A curated dataset comprising permissions associated with malicious applications will be employed, allowing for a comparative analysis against permissions extracted from the application under analysis. Through this approach, users will gain insights into the extent of malicious permissions embedded within an application. Further analysis will be conducted through comment analysis, enriching the depth of our understanding. In the contemporary landscape, detection techniques for smartphone devices have lagged behind the rapid proliferation of the mobile population. Recent surveys highlight the vast presence of approximately 2.1 million Android applications on the market, underscoring the need for an enhanced approach to combat the surge of Android malware. This influx of malware can be attributed to the burgeoning use of the Android system and the subsequent proliferation of applications developed by third parties. Moreover, it's essential to acknowledge that the Google Android market, despite its popularity, cannot guarantee the absolute absence of threats within its listed applications. Reports of Trojan applications with concealed malicious code further emphasise the necessity for more effective detection mechanisms, particularly during the app publication process in the Google Android market.

articleTitle: Deep Dive into IIoT Intrusion Detection Systems: A Review and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has quickly become a cutting-edge technology that can transform various sectors by digitalizing and connecting them, boosting business opportunities and global economic growth. Sectors like manufacturing, logistics, transportation, energy, and aviation are increasingly adopting IIoT. However, IIoT is vulnerable to cyber threats, requiring robust security measures. The numerous sensors in IIoT systems generate vast amounts of data, attracting cybercriminals. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS), which observe network traffic to detect unusual behavior, is crucial for securing IIoT applications. Recently, machine learning and deep learning techniques have shown potential in mitigating security threats and enhancing IDS performance. This paper reviews different deep learning-based IDS methods for IIoT, including techniques, datasets, and comparative analysis, and highlights existing limitations and future research directions.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Music Streaming Services: A Novel Approach to Transparent Artist Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Artists have historically used music as a form of personal expression. However, due to the centralized nature of music streaming services, artists receive only a small percentage of the revenue generated and have no control over their content produced. To address these issues, a revolutionary technique is needed that provides artists with greater control and transparency over their output. This paper focuses on a decentralized strategy that utilizes blockchain technology to facilitate direct interaction between artists and users, enabling artists to upload their music, sell songs, and receive royalties. The implementation of blockchain technology could potentially revolutionize the music industry by ensuring that rightful owners receive payment for their music while reducing the waste of paying intermediaries. Without intermediaries involved in the distribution process, the music industry could pay out more royalties to rights holders automatically and instantaneously. The proposed solution also addresses piracy concerns through the use of encryption and watermarking techniques. Blockchains provide security, confidentiality, tamper-proofing, traceability, control, and oversight over information. By developing a secure, self-installing, cross-platform reader positioned on the header of the digital content file, The research empowers data owners to manage the flow of information even after it has been made available. The suggested approach enables content owners to control their digital content and monitor its most popular components after distribution. The blockchain-based system also benefits from token distribution among the content’s owner, distributor, and consumer. The simulation results demonstrate that our approach is capable of overcoming the flaws of the existing system.

articleTitle: Blockchain Powered Carbon Credit Trading System using CAP-and-Trade Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Blockchain and Distributed Systems Security (ICBDS)
abstract: Climate change is the greatest long term threat that the global Community is currently facing. In response, many countries are submitting enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) to the UN, committing to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 2030. The Energy and Environmental Department at the National-level government wanted to create price incentives for industries to reduce their GHG emissions and stimulate investment in green innovation. To support these efforts, the proposed solution aims to develop a fully-functional, automatic and blockchain-powered Carbon trading platform that enables market participants to track, manage and trade GHG Credits (often referred to as Carbon Credits) while also helping the government to verily actual emission reductions. Blockchain-based architecture ensures that emissions data is tamper-proof, auditable securely recorded, enhancing accountability and participant trust. The carbon trading platform runs on CAP-and-Trade mechanism which is Government regulated Compliance market, in which specific sectors and Companies (usually called as obligated entities) are designated allowed to generate a certain volume of emissions (i.e. a CAP, carbon emission limit, acts as a Carbon emission Allowance Permit for these carbon emitters). If they exceed this limit, they may purchase Carbon Credits from environmental projects or have to pay carbon heavy taxes.
